meanings.note: Used in rhetorical or surprised questions.

examples.trans: How have you been?
How did you get here?
You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?
Everyone knows.
All preparations are finished.
Various age groups watch this program.
What is the main age group?

meanings.note: Often used for eating balanced foods or distributing things fairly.

examples.trans: Please eat a balanced variety of foods.
The scores came out evenly.

meanings.note: Short negation adverb placed before a verb or adjective.

examples.trans: I'm not going home today.
I haven't watched that movie.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch, to look

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
See you at the office tomorrow.
Director, I have something to tell you for a moment.
The director is in the conference room.
Please sit here.
This is our office.

meanings.en: to rise sharply, to surge, to spike

examples.trans: The ratings suddenly spiked sharply.
The temperature is rising sharply.

meanings.note: Used for time, distance, or chart intervals.

examples.trans: Traffic is very congested in this section.
I checked the high segment on the graph.

있다.gloss: to exist, there is, to have

meanings.en: to exist, to be present, there is

examples.trans: There is coffee on the desk.
Do you have time this afternoon?

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: Now the game is over.
I played a game with friends.

meanings.en: to end, to finish, to be over

examples.trans: The meeting is already over.
What time does class end?

meanings.note: Ra Joon-mo, the main variety PD in The Producers.

examples.trans: Joon-mo, come over here for a second.
Joon-mo is a variety department PD.

meanings.note: Often used adverbially without a particle or with topic particle -은.

examples.trans: The weather is really nice nowadays.
I'm busy these days so I can't exercise.

examples.text: 요즘은 볼 수 있는 매체가 많아요.
examples.trans: Nowadays there are many media outlets you can watch.
New media channels keep emerging.

많다.gloss: to be many, to be much

meanings.en: to be many, numerous, a lot

examples.trans: I have a lot of work to do today.
There are too many people on the street.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral, used for decimals, dates, money, etc.

examples.trans: The ratings came out at five percent.
Please wait just five minutes.

meanings.note: Used when reading decimal numbers, e.g. 오 점 칠 (5.7).

examples.text: 이번 주 시청률은 오 점 칠이에요.
examples.trans: This week's ratings are five point seven.
I learned many good points.
I'm going on vacation in July.
A week is seven days.

meanings.en: the old days, old times, the past

examples.trans: In the old days, this neighborhood was quiet.
Sometimes I think of the old days.
It starts in fifteen minutes.
Today is May fifteenth.

되다.gloss: to become, to amount to, to work

meanings.en: to amount to, to equal (a number/value)

examples.trans: It's already twelve o'clock.
Altogether it comes to 150,000 won.
Please take a look at this.
How much is this?

meanings.note: 답이 없다 ('there is no answer') is a common idiom meaning a situation is hopeless.

examples.trans: There's really no answer to this problem.
I found the answer to the question.

없다.gloss: to not exist, there is no, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, there is no

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
There is no milk in the fridge.

접다.gloss: to fold, to wrap up, to shut down

meanings.en: to wrap up, to shut down, to give up (a project or business)

examples.trans: Fold the paper in half.
Let's just scrap this project.
The bus has already left.
I already heard that news.

meanings.note: Pairs with 나다 (결정 나다, 'a decision is reached') or 하다 (결정하다, 'to decide').

examples.trans: A decision hasn't been reached yet.
I have to make an important decision.

meanings.note: Used before verbs to show completion (다 끝나다, 결정 다 나다).

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
All my friends came.

나다.gloss: to come out, to occur, to be reached

meanings.en: to come out, to arise, to occur
to be reached / finalized (with 결정, 결론, etc.)

examples.trans: A conclusion was finally reached.
I suddenly had a good idea.

meanings.note: Commonly used in official or workplace contexts.

examples.trans: It's a matter that has already been decided.
If you have any questions, please ask.

meanings.note: Used by a younger male to address an older brother or close older male friend/colleague.

examples.trans: Hey, do you have time tonight?
My older brother is an office worker.

meanings.en: to know, to be aware of

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.
Everyone in the variety department gathered.
I work in the variety department.

meanings.en: the whole, the entire thing, all

examples.trans: The entire team worked hard together.
Please check the entire schedule again.
Why do you think so?
Why didn't you answer the phone yesterday?

meanings.note: Informal 2nd-person pronoun used with close friends or juniors.

examples.trans: Do you have time today?
I'll count only on you.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of

examples.trans: I didn't know that fact.
If there are words you don't know, please ask.
Let's meet again next time.
I'm going on a business trip next week.
